nodes.summary: The complex $2 \times 2$ matrix with rows $(0, 1)$ and $(-1, 0)$ lies in the special unitary group $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ of complex $2 \times 2$ matrices.
nodes.title: The matrix with rows $(0, 1)$ and $(-1, 0)$ is special unitary

nodes.summary: The complex diagonal matrix $\operatorname{diag}(i, -i)$, where $i$ is the imaginary unit, lies in the special unitary group $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ of complex $2 \times 2$ matrices.
nodes.title: The matrix $\operatorname{diag}(i, -i)$ is special unitary

nodes.summary: For every real number $\theta$ and every integer $n$, the diagonal rotation through $\theta + 2\pi n$ equals the diagonal rotation through $\theta$.
nodes.title: Diagonal rotations are $2\pi$-periodic

nodes.summary: For real numbers $a$ and $b$, the diagonal rotations through $a$ and through $b$ are equal if and only if $a = b + 2\pi n$ for some integer $n$.
nodes.title: When two diagonal rotations are equal

nodes.summary: For every real number $\theta$, the diagonal rotation through $\theta$ is the diagonal matrix whose diagonal entries are $e^{i\theta}$ and $e^{-i\theta}$, in that order.
nodes.title: Diagonal rotations as diagonal matrices

nodes.summary: For every integer $n$, the diagonal rotation through $2\pi n$ is the $2 \times 2$ identity matrix.
nodes.title: Diagonal rotation through a multiple of $2\pi$

nodes.summary: For every real number $\theta$, the diagonal rotation through $\theta$ is a $2 \times 2$ complex matrix that is unitary and has determinant $1$, that is, it lies in $\mathrm{SU}(2)$.
nodes.title: Diagonal rotations lie in $\mathrm{SU}(2)$

nodes.summary: For real numbers $a$ and $b$, if the diagonal rotations through $a$ and through $b$ are equal as matrices, then the elements of the longitude subgroup given by the diagonal rotations through $a$ and through $b$ are equal.
nodes.title: Equal rotation matrices give equal longitude elements

nodes.summary: The homomorphism from the additive group $\mathbb{R}$ to the longitude subgroup, written additively, that sends a real number $\theta$ to the diagonal rotation through $\theta$, regarded as an element of the longitude subgroup.
nodes.title: The angle homomorphism into the longitude subgroup

nodes.summary: For real numbers $a$ and $b$, in the longitude subgroup the product of the diagonal rotations through $a$ and through $b$ is the diagonal rotation through $a + b$.
nodes.title: Longitude elements multiply by adding angles

nodes.summary: For a real number $\theta$, the diagonal rotation through $\theta$, regarded as an element of the longitude subgroup of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$.
nodes.title: Diagonal rotation as a longitude element

nodes.summary: For a real number $\theta$, the diagonal rotation through $\theta$ is the $2 \times 2$ complex diagonal matrix $\operatorname{diag}(e^{i\theta}, e^{-i\theta})$.
nodes.title: Diagonal rotation

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a complex $2 \times 2$ matrix in the special unitary group $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, that is, $M$ is unitary with determinant $1$. Then there are complex numbers $a, b$ with $|a|^2 + |b|^2 = 1$ such that the first row of $M$ is $(a, b)$ and the second row of $M$ is $(-\bar b, \bar a)$.
nodes.title: Matrix form of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$

nodes.summary: Every element $x$ of the circle group $\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z}$, written multiplicatively, is the class of some real number $a$.
nodes.title: Every point of $\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z}$ comes from a real angle

nodes.summary: For every real number $\theta$, the longitude map sends the class of $\theta$ in $\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z}$ to the diagonal rotation through $\theta$, regarded as an element of the longitude subgroup.
nodes.title: The longitude map on the class of an angle

nodes.summary: The longitude map from the circle group $\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z}$, written multiplicatively, to the longitude subgroup of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ is bijective.
nodes.title: The longitude map is bijective

nodes.summary: The longitude map from the circle group $\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z}$, written multiplicatively, to the longitude subgroup of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ is injective.
nodes.title: The longitude map is injective

nodes.summary: The longitude map from the circle group $\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z}$, written multiplicatively, to the longitude subgroup of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ is surjective: every element of the longitude subgroup is the image of some class.
nodes.title: The longitude map is surjective

nodes.summary: The longitude map is the group homomorphism from the circle group $\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z}$, written multiplicatively, to the longitude subgroup of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ that sends the class of a real number $\theta$ to the diagonal rotation through $\theta$, that is, to $\cos\theta \cdot I + \sin\theta \cdot \operatorname{diag}(i, -i) = \operatorname{diag}(e^{i\theta}, e^{-i\theta})$, where $I$ is the $2 \times 2$…
nodes.title: Longitude map

nodes.summary: The group isomorphism from the circle group $\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z}$, written multiplicatively, onto the longitude subgroup of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ given by the longitude map, which sends the class of a real number $\theta$ to the diagonal rotation through $\theta$.
nodes.title: Isomorphism of the circle group with the longitude subgroup

nodes.summary: The longitude subgroup of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ is the subgroup of those elements of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ that are the diagonal rotation through $\theta$ for some real number $\theta$.
nodes.title: Longitude subgroup

nodes.summary: An element $M$ of the special unitary group $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ of complex $2 \times 2$ matrices lies in the center of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ if and only if $M$ is the identity matrix $I$ or $M = -I$.
nodes.title: The center of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$

nodes.summary: A complex $2 \times 2$ matrix $M$ lies in the special unitary group $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, that is, $M$ is unitary with determinant $1$, if and only if there are complex numbers $\alpha, \beta$ with $|\alpha|^2 + |\beta|^2 = 1$ such that the first row of $M$ is $(\alpha, \beta)$ and the second row is $(-\bar\beta, \bar\alpha)$.
nodes.title: Characterization of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$

nodes.summary: For every complex $2 \times 2$ matrix $M$ in the special unitary group $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, the trace of $M$ satisfies $|\operatorname{tr} M| \le 2$.
nodes.title: The trace of an $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ matrix has absolute value at most two

nodes.summary: For every real number $\theta$, the conjugate transpose of the diagonal rotation through $\theta$ is the diagonal rotation through $-\theta$.
nodes.title: Conjugate transpose of a diagonal rotation

nodes.summary: The center of the special unitary group $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ of complex $2 \times 2$ matrices is not all of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$.
nodes.title: The center of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ is proper

nodes.summary: Two elements of `SU₂` with the same trace are conjugate in `SU₂`.
nodes.title: Conjugacy in `SU₂` is determined by the trace

nodes.summary: Every element of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ is conjugate in $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ to an element of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ that is the diagonal matrix $\operatorname{diag}(z, \bar z)$ for some complex number $z$ with $z \bar z = 1$.
nodes.title: Diagonalization in $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ up to conjugacy

nodes.summary: Let $z_1, z_2$ be complex numbers with $z_1 \bar z_1 = 1$ and $z_2 \bar z_2 = 1$, and let $D_1, D_2$ be elements of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ equal to the diagonal matrices $\operatorname{diag}(z_1, \bar z_1)$ and $\operatorname{diag}(z_2, \bar z_2)$. If $D_1$ and $D_2$ have the same trace, then they are conjugate in $\mathrm{SU}(2)$.
nodes.title: Diagonal elements of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ with equal trace are conjugate

nodes.summary: For all $P$ and $A$ in $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, the trace of $P A P^{-1}$ equals the trace of $A$.
nodes.title: Trace is invariant under conjugation in $\mathrm{SU}(2)$

nodes.summary: For every complex $2 \times 2$ matrix $M$ in the special unitary group $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, the imaginary part of the trace of $M$ is $0$.
nodes.title: The trace of an $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ matrix is real

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
